programme: PPARG and PPARD (PPAR-family lipid-sensing nuclear receptors, with CREBL2 acting directly on PPARG and its adipogenic/macrophage-differentiation partner CEBPA) driving fatty-acid handling and macrophage polarization, paired with HEY1, the Notch-effector bHLH factor that sets endothelial/vascular smooth-muscle state.
role_in_a: In lung cancer, PPARG-dependent fatty-acid oxidation supports tumor cell and tumor-associated-macrophage metabolism (PMID 41866994, PMID 42294275), the PPARG-FABP4 axis reprograms macrophage endoplasmic-reticulum stress in the tumor microenvironment (PMID 41317938), and the Notch effector HEY1 drives EMT-linked cisplatin resistance in adenocarcinoma (PMID 36396748) — together a lipid-metabolic/Notch programme that supports tumor and stromal cell survival and chemoresistance.
role_in_b: In stroke, the same lipid-handling axis operates in the vessel wall: PPARG-linked control of macrophage efferocytosis governs atherosclerotic plaque stability, the proximate lesion behind large-vessel ischemic stroke (PMID 40356342), PPARG pathways are implicated in post-stroke cognitive recovery (PMID 41996726), and HEY1 preserves brain vascular endothelial function and limits ischemic injury (PMID 35316462) — a plaque-macrophage/endothelial-protective role for the same factors.
shared_axis: Both diseases depend on how myeloid and vascular cells in blood and lung handle lipids and Notch signaling: the PPARG/PPARD-CREBL2 node sets macrophage lipid uptake and polarization (tumor-associated macrophages in lung cancer, plaque macrophages in atherosclerotic stroke), while HEY1-Notch sets the endothelial/smooth-muscle state that either supports tumor vasculature and EMT or protects against ischemic endothelial injury — the same nuclear-receptor/Notch circuitry read out in opposite tissue contexts of a shared myeloid-vascular biology.
reasoning: PPARG and HEY1 each have disease-specific primary papers independently placing them in lung cancer and in stroke-relevant vascular pathology, and PPARD's high Open Targets percentile in both diseases is consistent with the same family acting in both tissues, so the module is nameable and largely placed. But no retrieved source connects lung cancer and stroke through these factors jointly, and CREBL2 has no disease association at all and is included only because its two known targets are CEBPA and PPARG — so the cross-disease link rests on reasoning about shared macrophage/vascular biology, not on anything retrieved.
support: PMID 41866994 — PPARG-dependent fatty acid oxidation targeted by (-)-Guaiol in lung cancer; PMID 42294275 — plant EV-like particles suppress lung cancer via a PPARG-linked route; PMID 41317938 — PPARG-FABP4 reprograms tumor-associated macrophage ER stress in lung cancer; PMID 40356342 — PPARG-linked macrophage efferocytosis defect promotes atherosclerotic plaque instability (stroke substrate); PMID 41996726 — PPARG-associated compound mechanism in post-stroke cognitive impairment; PMID 36396748 — HEY1 drives EMT-mediated cisplatin resistance in lung adenocarcinoma; PMID 35316462 — HEY1 improves brain vascular endothelial function and alleviates ischemic stroke.
how_to_falsify: Knock down PPARG (and separately PPARD) in a lung tumor-associated-macrophage co-culture and in a plaque-macrophage/foam-cell model from the same patient's monocytes; if fatty-acid oxidation/efferocytosis phenotypes and HEY1-dependent endothelial or EMT readouts do not shift concordantly across both systems, the shared-axis claim fails. A complementary test: ChIP or CUT&RUN for PPARG and HEY1 in matched blood myeloid cells from lung cancer and stroke cohorts to check whether they actually co-occupy CEBPA/PPARG-adjacent lipid-handling loci in both settings, rather than merely being separately associated with each disease.
caveats: Support is built from 84 patient-group comparisons but only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance fraction is inflated by within-cohort repetition rather than independent replication. Blood|lung tissue pairing plausibly reflects circulating/tissue-resident myeloid biology, consistent with a macrophage-centered axis, but PPARD and CREBL2 carry no disease-specific papers, only association-percentile or target-overlap inference. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed the more obvious macrophage/endothelial master regulators (EPAS1, IRF8, BCL6, CREB5, ETS2, ID2/ID3, STAT1, FOXO1, ERG) precisely because they are ordinary for blood/lung tissue — PPARG, PPARD and HEY1 stood out above that generic background, which is why they, not those factors, anchor this account. About half the factors in the full list (CXXC1, ZKSCAN7, PHF20, ZNF451, GABPA, CREB3L1, ISL1, THAP1) returned no evidence tying them to this specific programme and were excluded from the mechanistic account rather than forced into it.
